title: EmpireMap state dossier
description: One state's dossier for the EmpireMap historical-borders project (history/master-plan.md, 'Collection method'): identity, a review of its Cliopatria keyframe shapes, a dated ledger of territorial events, its wars, the certainty of its borders per era, and every source opened. Years are integers, negative for BCE, as in Cliopatria; a month is 1..12 where the record supports it. Regions are named with the shared region grammar ($defs/region), never drawn. File name: history/polities/<identity.slug>.json. Validate with tools/validate_dossier.py.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, so editors can validate the file; any string.

identity.description: Who the state is: names, type, family, life span, neighbours in time (predecessors and successors), capitals and, where a documented list exists, rulers.

slug.description: The dossier's identifier and file name: tools/slug.py slugify() of the Cliopatria Name, as it stands in data/polities.csv (which adds -2, -3 where two Names collide); for a state Cliopatria lacks, slugify() of the dossier name.

name.description: The display name, in English, as the map labels it ('Tang dynasty', 'Kingdom of France').

native_names.description: Names in the state's own languages and scripts, with a romanisation where the script is not Latin ('唐', 'Táng'); empty list when none is recorded.

alt_names.description: Other English names and spellings a reader might search for ('Tang Empire', 'Great Tang'); the site's search uses them; empty list when none.

type.description: What kind of entity the dossier describes. state: a sovereign polity. dynasty: a state named for its ruling house (the Chinese, Persian and Indian dynasties), drawn exactly like a state; a dynasty that merely succeeds another on the same land without a break is not a new dossier (master plan rule 2). culture: an archaeological culture before 3400 BCE, drawn muted and dotted, never as a state. colony: a dependency ruled from elsewhere, drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole. rebel: a rebel or civil-war state (An Lushan's Yan, the Taiping), drawn hatched in its own colour until it wins or is crushed. umbrella: an association or empire-wide entity that is not territory of its own (Cliopatria's parenthesised names: the Holy Roman Empire after 1648, the Commonwealth), never coloured as territory.

family.description: The civilisation family the colour registry draws the state's hue from: a key of colours.json 'families' (china, rome, caliphate, persia, steppe, india, korea, japan, france, britain, ...). Successors that claim continuity share the family.

cliopatria_names.description: The Cliopatria Name values (verbatim, case and diacritics kept) whose shapes this dossier reviews; empty list for a state Cliopatria lacks; more than one when the researcher merges Cliopatria rows into one state.

wikipedia.description: The English Wikipedia article title of the state ('Tang dynasty'), as Cliopatria's Wikipedia field gives it; null when there is none.

wikidata.description: The Wikidata id ('Q9683') from Cliopatria; null when there is none. Wikidata itself is unreachable from the agents; the id is kept for the site's links.

start.description: When the state begins: its founding, with the month when the record gives one. The map draws the state from this year (rule 1, birth).

end.description: When the state ends (dissolution, conquest, partition), with the month when known; for a state alive today, the current year. The map draws the state through this year (rule 7, collapse).

predecessors.description: The states whose land this state took at its birth, each with the land handed over; empty list for a state that arose on nobody's land.

successors.description: The states that took this state's land at its end, each with the land handed over; empty list for a state alive today or whose land returned to nobody.

capitals.description: Every capital in turn, with coordinates and years; the map draws the capital as a dot that moves (rule 10). At least one entry for every state that had a seat of government; empty list only for cultures and stateless entities.

items.description: One capital for one span of years.

name.description: The capital's name as the sources of the period give it, with the modern name in parentheses where it differs ('Chang'an (Xi'an)').

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, WGS84, east positive.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, WGS84, north positive.

from.description: First year this city was the capital.

to.description: Last year this city was the capital (inclusive).

source.description: URL of the page that gives the capital and its years; optional when the identity's Wikipedia article is the source.

note.description: Anything the reader should know (a second capital, a court in exile, a renaming).

rulers.description: The ruler strip (rule 10): only for states with a documented list (China, Rome, the caliphates, Europe from about 800); omit the key otherwise. Reign years, in order, one entry per reign; an interregnum ruler (Wu Zetian) is listed in place.

name.description: The ruler as the map labels them: temple, regnal or personal name ('Taizong (Li Shimin)').

title.description: The title where it is not the state's usual one (regent, empress regnant, co-emperor).

source.description: URL of the page the list was read from; give it on the first entry at least.

note.description: A disputed date, a deposition, a second reign.

keyframe_review.description: One entry per Cliopatria shape of this state (data/shapes.csv rows with this slug, or data/polities/<slug>.json shapes[]), plus one entry per new keyframe for a period Cliopatria lacks. Every verdict cites the page it rests on.

items.description: The verdict on one keyframe shape.

shape_id.description: The shape's id from data/shapes.csv: slug + '_' + FromYear (+ a letter when two shapes share a FromYear), e.g. 'tang-dynasty_705'. For a new keyframe, the same form with the new FromYear ('tang-dynasty_618'); the validator treats an id absent from shapes.csv as new and then requires 'from' and 'to'.

verdict.description: ok: the shape is right for its years as drawn (within the honest precision of the era). adjust: the shape is broadly right but should be corrected as 'correction' says. wrong: the shape should not be used for these years; 'correction' gives the shape to use instead, or the years it belongs to.

correction.description: Required for adjust and wrong (and for a new keyframe): the shape as it should be, written as a region spec with 'text' in the source's own words. Describe the whole corrected shape, not the delta: {'minus': [{'cliopatria': Name, 'year': y}, X]} removes X from the Cliopatria shape, {'union': [{'cliopatria': ...}, Y]} adds Y. A verdict that only changes the years says so in 'text' and gives the shape unchanged.

from.description: New keyframes only: the first year the described shape holds.

to.description: New keyframes only: the last year the described shape holds (inclusive).

source.description: URL of the page the verdict rests on; a page listed in 'sources'.

note.description: Why, in one or two sentences: what the page says, how far the area is from the infobox, what the rendering agent should expect.

verdict.description: Selector: an adjust or wrong verdict.

ledger.description: The dated territorial events, in year order (then month). Every border move between two keyframes is explained by at least one event; every event names its region in words, its counterpart, the page it came from and a confidence. The rendering agents apply these year by year; 'note' doubles as the map caption.

year.description: The year of the event (negative for BCE). A process spread over years gets one event per dated step, or one event at the decisive date with the span in 'note'.

month.description: The month (1..12) where the record gives one; omit otherwise. Months are stored so a monthly step can be added later without re-collecting.

type.description: found: the state appears on its core (rule 1). gain / loss: land taken from or given to 'counterpart' ('nobody' when it was stateless). contest_start / contest_end: fighting over 'region' between this state and 'counterpart' begins (first campaign that takes or holds ground) or ends (treaty, last battle, de facto end); the zone is drawn in the blend (rule 6). vassal_start / vassal_end: 'region' (usually a whole state) becomes or ceases to be this state's vassal, protectorate, tributary or client, drawn in the lighter tint (rule 4); 'counterpart' is the vassal itself in both events (the same string, so the validator can pair them), and a conqueror who ends the relation goes in 'note'. occupation_start / occupation_end: this state occupies 'region' belonging to 'counterpart' without annexing it, hatched (rule 4); the owner records the same event with the roles reversed. capital_move: the seat moves (rule 10; the destination in 'note' and in identity.capitals). rename: the state changes its name or a dynasty changes within the same state (Tang to Zhou to Tang); colour and dossier continue (rule 2). split: part of the state becomes a new state named in 'counterpart'. merge: this state absorbs or is absorbed into 'counterpart'. dissolve: the state ends; its land goes to identity.successors (rule 7).

region.description: The land the event concerns, as a region spec (the shared grammar) with 'text' giving the source's own words. Required for every type except rename and capital_move.

counterpart.description: The other party: the slug of its dossier when one exists or will exist (data/polities.csv slugs; the slug rule for new states), otherwise its name as the source gives it; 'nobody' for stateless land. Required for gain, loss, contest_*, vassal_*, occupation_* and merge.

source.description: URL of the page the event was read from; it must appear in 'sources'. One page per event; put a second page in 'note'.

confidence.description: 3: the page dates the event and names the land in its own words. 2: the year is the page's, the region is the researcher's reading of it (a province named from a city, a span rounded to a year). 1: the researcher's bridging judgment where the page is silent (a date inferred from a Cliopatria shape, a region inferred from a later state of affairs); the reviewer treats 1 as a gap to fill.

note.description: One sentence a viewer can read as the caption ('618: Li Yuan proclaims the Tang at Chang'an'), then anything else: the page's wording, a disagreement between pages, the span of a drawn-out process.

type.description: Selector: every type except rename and capital_move.
Selector: the types that need a counterpart.

wars.description: The wars that moved or threatened this state's borders: name, years, every belligerent, the zones fought over (which feed the contested-territory rule) and the outcome. A war with no territorial result is still listed (so the reviewer can see it was considered) with empty zones.

name.description: The war's usual English name, as the Wikipedia article titles it.

to.description: Last year of fighting or the treaty year (inclusive).

belligerents.description: Every party, this state included: dossier slugs where they exist, otherwise names as the source gives them.

items.description: One belligerent: a slug or a name.

zones.description: The land fought over and held or changed hands, as region specs ('text' recommended); empty when the war moved no border. The ledger's contest_start / contest_end events reference the same zones.

outcome.description: The result in one or two sentences: who won, what changed hands, the treaty.

source.description: URL of the page the war was read from; it must appear in 'sources'.

note.description: Anything else: disagreements between pages, a front that moved year by year (give the years), why a zone is or is not contested.

certainty.description: How certain the state's borders are, per era, covering the whole life without gaps: sharp (treaty or survey lines) or soft (approximate frontiers: steppe, forest, desert, most of the ancient world). Drives the edge style (rule 9); 'note' names the borders that differ from the era's level.

level.description: sharp: borders fixed by treaty, survey or a dated administrative record. soft: approximate frontiers, drawn soft or dashed.

note.description: Which borders are the exception to the era's level, and why ('the Tibetan frontier is sharp after the 783 treaty; the steppe frontier is soft throughout').

sources.description: Every page opened for this dossier, with its URL and the date it was read. A search snippet is not a source. Every 'source' URL in the dossier must appear here.

url.description: The page's URL, exactly as opened.

accessed.description: The date the page was read, YYYY-MM-DD.

note.description: What the page was used for, or why it was thin (a redirect, a stub, a page that would not load and was replaced).

notes.description: Free text for what the researcher could not settle: Cliopatria rows to split or merge, states that need their own dossier (rebels, protectorates), disagreements between pages, pages that would not load. The reviewer and the gap-fillers read it first.

slug.description: A dossier identifier by the shared slug rule (tools/slug.py): lower-case ASCII letters and digits separated by single hyphens, with the prefix 'rel-' for a Cliopatria umbrella or relation entity.

year.description: An integer year, negative for BCE (−6000 is the project's first year), with no year 0 issue: Cliopatria's convention is followed as it stands.

date.description: A year with an optional month.

month.description: The month, where the record gives one.

url.description: An http(s) URL of a page that was opened.

text.description: The source's own words for the region ('the Four Garrisons of Anxi', 'the Hexi Corridor from Liangzhou to Dunhuang'); free text, ignored by the gazetteer, kept for the reviewer and the state page.

handover.description: A predecessor or successor and the land that passed between it and this state.

slug.description: The other state's dossier slug (an existing slug from data/polities.csv, or the slug rule applied to the name of a state that still needs a dossier).

land.description: The land handed over, as a region spec; {'cliopatria': Name, 'year': y} of the other state's first or last shape is the usual form; 'text' recommended.

note.description: Anything else: a date that differs from the start or end year, a partial handover.

region_text.description: A region spec that must carry 'text', the source's own words.

region.description: The shared region grammar (gazetteer, dossier schema and briefs): a named region, never drawn coordinates except the 12-point fallback. Exactly one form applies; any form may also carry 'text'. Country and admin-1 spellings follow Natural Earth 10m (data/gazetteer/countries.jsonl and admin1.jsonl names or alt_names); historical regions are the entries of data/gazetteer/regions.jsonl; places are data/gazetteer/places.jsonl. Resolve with tools/gazetteer.py. The river and lake forms are gazetteer extensions of the grammar.

oneOf.description: A modern country by its Natural Earth name.

country.description: Natural Earth 10m admin-0 name (ADMIN or NAME) or a listed alias ('China', 'Czechia', 'United States of America').

oneOf.description: A first-level administrative unit of a modern country (province, state, oblast).

admin1.description: Natural Earth 10m admin-1 name or alias ('Gansu', 'Xinjiang', 'Bavaria'); a Natural Earth 'region' value (an Italian region) also works.

country.description: The unit's country, by its Natural Earth name.

oneOf.description: A radius around a named place.

place.description: A populated place from data/gazetteer/places.jsonl, by name or alias ('Kucha', 'Chang'an', 'Samarkand').

country.description: The place's modern country, to disambiguate a repeated name (Dali in Shaanxi or in Yunnan).

oneOf.description: A radius around a coordinate; use only when no place name will do.
A polity's Cliopatria shape in a given year (the shape alive in that year).

cliopatria.description: The Cliopatria Name, verbatim ('Tang Dynasty', 'Tibetan Empire').

year.description: A year in which the polity has a shape; that shape is used.

region.description: An entry of data/gazetteer/regions.jsonl by name or alias ('Tarim Basin', 'Hexi Corridor', 'Transoxiana', 'Aquitaine'); an unknown name goes to the gazetteer agent, who adds it.

oneOf.description: A fallback polygon of at most 12 points, only when no name will do.

polygon.description: The ring as [lon, lat] pairs, 3 to 12 points, not closed.

oneOf.description: A band along the border between two states in a year, for sources that say only 'the frontier'.

border_band.description: The two states, the year whose border is taken, and the band's width in cells on either side.

year.description: The year whose border between a and b is taken.

width.description: Width of the band in H3 cells on each side of the border (1 or 2 is usual).

oneOf.description: The union of two or more regions.
The first region minus the second.

minus.description: Exactly two regions: [A, B] gives A without B.

oneOf.description: The intersection of two or more regions.
Gazetteer extension: the cells a river passes through, widened by a radius.

river.description: A river from data/gazetteer/rivers.jsonl by name or alias ('Yellow', 'Amu Darya').

km.description: How far from the centreline to include, in kilometres; 0 for the line's own cells.

oneOf.description: Gazetteer extension: the cells of a lake (lakes are land cells in this grid).

lake.description: A lake from data/gazetteer/lakes.jsonl by name or alias.
